chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuses the repentance of the one with bad manners.' It was said, 'And how is that so, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Because when he repents from a sin, he falls into a sin greater than it.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah refuse the repentance of those with bad manners?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) highlights a spiritual danger where persistent bad manners (khuluq sayyi') lead to a cycle of superficial repentance, causing one to trade minor sins for greater ones. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internalization of character (akhlaq) as a prerequisite for sincere tawbah, warning that without genuine transformation, ritual repentance may become a mere mechanism for avoiding accountability rather than a path to divine closeness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Refuses (to Accept) the repentance of the one of the evil manners with the repentance’. It was said, ‘And how is that so, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Because, when he repents from a sin, he falls into a sin more grievous than it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Holy Prophet has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, refuses to accept the repentance of a person of bad conduct.’ It was asked, ‘Why is it so, O Messenger of Allah?’ He said, ‘It is because when he repents from a sin he falls into a greater sin.’”
